Record Q1 2020 revenue of $28.2M (+95%) despite COVID-19 onset; company does not provide formal guidance.
Growth driven by North America (+70%), full-quarter Func Food consolidation in Europe, DSD network expansion (100+ partners), Walmart nationwide launch, and expanded Target assortment.
Gross margin expanded 660 bps to 46.1% on European consolidation mix and volume leverage; growth entirely volume-driven, not pricing.

COVID-19 shifted demand to online, curbside and pantry purchasing while halting experiential marketing (Live Fit Tour); company pivoted to online programs (SWEAT WITH CELSIUS virtual workouts, Barry's partnership).
Strategic inventory build of $5.5M (started late December) ahead of March/April retailer resets drove $3.8M cash outflow from operations.
Bang Energy's move to 100% Pepsi distribution frees up Anheuser-Busch independent distributors; management sees opportunity to capture distributor partners.
Stores transitioned to DSD (Target, 7-Eleven NY metro via Big Geyser) saw volumes more than double; ~40% sales-volume lift on top of ~30% same-store growth.
Walmart DSD conversion expected H2 2020; less than 10% of ~65,000 NA doors currently DSD-serviced — large runway.
Management maintains premium pricing position; will not discount as category continues to grow.
Big summer promotional programs planned with Target and 7-Eleven for July-August beverage season.
Func Food integration delivering synergies; protein bar line for North America delayed by COVID.
April North America orders up ~38%, providing confidence on momentum, though management declined to call it a floor given channel-reopening uncertainty.

Asked whether industry activity (Pepsi acquiring Rockstar, becoming distributor for Bang away from Anheuser) is shifting distribution conversations toward larger deals for Celsius; follow-up on whether Pepsi may become more promotional with Bang.

Bang's transition to 100% Pepsi creates opportunity for Celsius to gain distributor partners; transitions expected over ~60 days. Bang's exclusivity contracts had previously limited Celsius. Expects heavy promotional activity in summer beverage season (July-August); emphasized premium positioning and strong category pricing.
European volume, new flavors & Func integration
Asked about the spike in European volume outside the Nordics, the Peach Vibe limited edition rollout, the closing/integration of Func and North America snacks/bars, and the inventory build.

European growth driven mainly by Sweden (fastest-growing energy brand per Nielsen); Norway/Finland challenged by lockdowns. Peach Vibe rolling out on Amazon and into retailers as planograms reset. Func integration going well with further synergy opportunities; North America protein bar line delayed by COVID. Inventory increase ~$5.5M, mainly US, ~130 days of inventory — a deliberate strategic move.
Jeff Van Sinderen - B. Riley FBR
Asked for color on Walmart (~50% DSD), the DSD conversion path there and at Target, what is being seen in reopening U.S. regions, and how marketing plans are evolving.

DSD-serviced Walmart stores show better in-stocks/placements; confident more Walmarts flip to DSD in H2 2020. Target NY-metro Big Geyser stores show great velocities; 5 markets identified for conversion, big July promotional program planned. Declined to forecast reopening given week-by-week uncertainty; cited April orders up 38%. Marketing re-engineered toward online/social/e-commerce with cautious return to offline activation planned.
Asked whether total online business was positively impacted by COVID-19, what online/Amazon growth was, and to discuss COVID positives/negatives plus supply-chain contingency plans.

Online a strong long-term growth area with COVID-driven spikes; Celsius outpaced Monster and Red Bull. Celsius positioned as daily-routine product, not an impulse buy. Few real positives given the human toll; company donated thousands of cases to 450+ hospitals, set department contingency plans since January, built inventory, placed longer-dated blanket POs, and expanded the co-packer network.
Asked, given more limited distributor options, whether Celsius would consider distributors taking equity positions, and whether it would align with one major player versus a fragmented structure.
Deliberately non-specific — evaluating a variety of relationships, will do what is best for shareholders to drive Celsius to number one. Declined to discuss specific contract negotiations.
Online vs. retail mix, DSD penetration & April trend
Asked the bricks-and-mortar vs. online sales split, the % of doors DSD-serviced and shift pace over 12-24 months, whether the 40% DSD lift held across markets, and whether April +38% is a low mark.

No longer discloses online/retail split as retail partners' online businesses blur the line and Celsius does not sell direct. Of ~65,000 NA doors, less than 10% currently DSD-serviced, many flipping H2 2020. Confirmed ~40% DSD lift consistent (sometimes higher) across markets. Declined to forecast whether April +38% is a floor.
